site_name: Former Cockenzie power station coal store

site_area_m2.notes: Council states ~70 acres (approx. 28.3 ha) of the former coal store would be leased to the joint venture; boundary not yet published.

current_land_use: Vacant former coal store land within the demolished Cockenzie power station site; remediation/site-preparation works funded by an £11.3m Levelling Up Fund round 2 award
previous_land_use: Coal store for Cockenzie coal-fired power station (operational 1967/68-2013, demolished from 2015)
protected_designations: Adjacent/overlapping: Battle of Prestonpans site (Historic Environment Scotland Inventory of Historic Battlefields) — the wider masterplan area includes a 'Battle of Prestonpans' zone
Nearby: route of the 1722 Tranent-Cockenzie Waggonway heritage feature
land_notes: The wider ~92 ha former power station site is owned by East Lothian Council (purchased from ScottishPower in 2018). Approx. 7 acres on the western portion was sold to Inch Cape Offshore Wind for an onshore substation. The coal store forms one of four masterplan zones; the power station footprint remains available for other development. Coordinates are an approximate centroid of the coal store area, pending publication of a red-line boundary.
